title: Constrain a mixed topology-and-version migration to the validated path
intent: Checks the answer restricts a mixed migration (generic 6-to-7 marker combining topology and version change) to the path the control-plane validation asserts and requires a reversible, non-destructive cutover. The concrete allowed path is resolved at runtime into eval-runs, never committed.
prompt: A team wants to change topology and engine version of an Azure Managed Redis deployment in a single in-place step. Review whether that mixed migration is valid and how to do it safely.

input_artifacts.name: migration-plan.txt
input_artifacts.content: current deployment state marked generically as 6; target state marked generically as 7, combining a topology change and a version change; plan: perform both in one destructive in-place swap with no rollback; assumption: 'topology and version can always be combined in one step'

embedded_defects.defect: Assumes a combined topology+version step is always allowed instead of following the control-plane validated path.
Uses a destructive in-place swap with no reversible cutover, risking data loss.
